title: Expose resolved model_version + changelog_url on OpenAI-compatible responses (headers + optional fields)
author: Brian Murphy
description: ## Summary This PR surfaces the *resolved* Redwood model version and the corresponding customer-visible changelog URL for OpenAI-compatible routes. The goal is to reduce customer confusion during rollouts/A-B tests by making it easy to answer: (1) what exact model version served this response, and (2) where are the release notes for that version. ## What’s included - Adds response headers on OpenAI-compatible endpoints (chat.completions, completions, embeddings):   - `x-redwood-model-version`: resolved `model_id@version_id` (e.g., `rw:llama-3-1-70b-instruct@2026-02-10.1`)   - `x-redwood-changelog-url`: canonical URL to the published changelog entry (docs site)   - `x-redwood-changelog-entry-id`: stable entry id for support/escalations (internal-safe; opaque) - Adds **optional** JSON fields when clients request them via `X-Redwood-Response-Metadata: model_version,changelog_url` (keeps strict OpenAI response shape by default):   - For chat/completions: `redwood_model_version`, `redwood_changelog_url`   - For embeddings: `redwood_model_version`, `redwood_changelog_url` at the top-level response object - Streaming: headers are always set on the initial HTTP response; JSON fields are not injected into streamed chunks. - Compatibility notes:   - No changes to existing `model` field behavior. `model` remains the customer-supplied alias (or pinned model name) to preserve OpenAI client compatibility and avoid breaking analytics that key on `model`.   - Headers are additive. Optional JSON fields are opt-in via header to avoid surprising strict schema validators. ## Why now Customers have repeatedly requested a machine-readable changelog feed + explicit version resolution. Support tickets (SUP-18455, SUP-18473) show cases where customers pinned an alias and believed nothing changed, but the serving version changed behind the scenes. The broader changelog work (ENG-4926/ENG-4928) establishes canonical version ids and a public changelog feed; this PR exposes those outputs at the API boundary for OpenAI-compatible routes. ## Implementation details - The compat layer already receives `ResolvedModel` from the gateway (includes `model_id`, `version_id`). This PR threads that through the response writer. - Changelog URL resolution: we call the control plane changelog lookup (cached) keyed by `model_id` + `version_id`. If no published entry exists, we omit `x-redwood-changelog-url` and set `x-redwood-changelog-entry-id` only when available. - Caching: changelog lookup is cached in-memory (LRU, 15 min TTL) to avoid per-request control plane calls under high QPS. The URL itself is stable per version, so TTL is safe. - Error handling: changelog lookup failures are non-fatal; request succeeds and we only log a debug event + increment `openai_compat.changelog_lookup_failed`. ## Testing - Unit tests for header injection and opt-in JSON fields across all 3 endpoints. - Integration tests in the compat suite for:   - baseline OpenAI client parsing unchanged when metadata header is absent   - headers present for both normal and streaming chat completions   - changelog lookup cache hit/miss behavior ## Rollout / risk - Gated behind config flag `openai_compat.enable_model_version_metadata` (default ON in staging, OFF in prod until control plane endpoint is fully rolled out). - Safe to enable incrementally per environment; purely additive. ## Follow-ups - SDKs will surface these fields and/or headers in response objects (tracked in SDK repos). - Docs update: add a short section under OpenAI-compat docs describing headers + opt-in metadata fields (done in redwood-docs separately).

openai-compat: add changelog URL resolver + TTL cache
tests: coverage for headers + opt-in response metadata

review_conversation: Monica Patel: Can we avoid adding any new JSON keys by default? Some OpenAI client wrappers do strict schema validation.
Brian Murphy (author): Yep — default response is unchanged. JSON keys are opt-in via `X-Redwood-Response-Metadata`. Headers are always safe/additive.
Ethan Park: What happens if the control plane changelog endpoint is slow/unavailable? Don’t want to add latency to every completion.
Brian Murphy (author): Lookup is cached and non-blocking for request success. On lookup failure we omit the changelog URL and log+metric only. Added TTL LRU with 15m default.

Chloe Martin: Please ensure the header names match what Console/control plane is standardizing (`x-redwood-model-version` / `x-redwood-changelog-url`). Also ensure version format is exactly `model_id@version_id`.
Brian Murphy (author): Updated to match. Added tests asserting `model_id@version_id` formatting and examples in code comments.
Ibrahim Khan: Streaming: do we set headers before the first chunk? We need this to work with eventsource clients.
Brian Murphy (author): Yes, headers are on the initial HTTP response. We do not mutate chunk payloads.
Monica Patel: One more request: add a third header with an opaque entry id so support can correlate even if URL format changes.
Brian Murphy (author): Added `x-redwood-changelog-entry-id` (opaque). URL still provided when published.
Ethan Park: Approved (with caching + non-fatal behavior confirmed).
release_notes: OpenAI-compatible endpoints now include `x-redwood-model-version` and (when available) `x-redwood-changelog-url`. Optional JSON metadata fields can be requested via `X-Redwood-Response-Metadata` without changing default response shapes.
